expectations.text: report.pdf exists in outputs and has exactly 1 page
Response states the analysed period (months or dates)
Every growth/decline claim carries an uncertainty measure (interval or explicit confidence level)
expectations.evidence: Intervals and confidence for key series

expectations.text: Response names the Wikipedia articles (or article basket/proxies) that were measured
expectations.evidence: IELTS, TOEFL and 'English language' articles, with their intent explained

expectations.text: Response ranks or prioritises the five language audiences explicitly
expectations.evidence: Turkish and Vietnamese first, others explained

expectations.text: Ranking reasons use both audience size and growth (or intensity), not just one number
expectations.evidence: Uses views/month, intensity per 1M, relative growth and rank scores

expectations.text: Response mentions that a language edition is not the same as a country (or gives a reader-geography caveat)
expectations.evidence: Withheld home countries acknowledged; says most readers are probably in the country

expectations.text: Response notes that Wikipedia interest is not purchase intent or recommends validating with another signal
Does not describe a change whose 95% interval crosses zero as growth (e.g. Turkish +7% [-20%, +43%] is 'no clear change')
expectations.evidence: No '+x%' with an interval crossing zero is called growth; vi '+2% [-8%, +15%]' is described as a stable trend

expectations.text: Reasons are grounded in the data: no unsupported outside claims (competition, market size, demographics) or misreadings of the metrics presented as findings
expectations.evidence: Still frames '31% з США' as 'значна частина трафіку — з діаспори' (the shares only split non-withheld traffic) and calls the Turkish lead 'явне домінування' despite LOW confidence
